sentence: This project studies whether clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential is linked to sudden cardiac death, using blood and heart samples from autopsy-confirmed cases.
This project builds a shared data service that manages and analyzes clinical, microbiome, and multi-omics data to help study infections from antibiotic resistant pathogens.
This project analyzes RNA sequencing data and functional assay data to help understand and treat atrial fibrillation.
This project tries to find out how hormone receptors keep breast cancer cells in a dormant state, so that late tumor recurrence can be prevented.
This project studies how a long noncoding RNA helps repair damaged telomeres and how that repair can cause telomeres to fuse together.
This project provides tissue sectioning, staining, and slide analysis services that help cancer researchers study tumors in vertebrate model organisms.
This project studies how microbiota and the immune system affect nerve overgrowth in the skin and how that relates to itch.
This project builds an atomic force microscopy method that measures how strongly cancer cells and tissue samples attract and what drives their surface adhesiveness.
This project studies impulsive behaviors in youth at risk for Huntington disease to see whether they are an early sign of the disease.
This project studies the basic principles that govern protein aggregation across many neurodegenerative diseases, including those that follow traumatic brain injury.
This project uses computational methods and systems models to process large data and test hypotheses about how biological processes function.
This project tries to find out how chronic pancreatitis leads to diabetes by studying signaling and genetic changes in islet cells.
This project tests a way to find tumor-specific antigens and grow tumor-specific T cells to treat invasive brain cancers called pediatric high-grade gliomas.
This project builds secreted fluorescent biosensors that can image the space outside cells in living organisms.
This project provides source cells from subjects with neurological disorders such as Parkinson’s disease and Alzheimer’s disease for other scientists to use.
This project studies how parts of the ventral stream of the visual system respond and models them to predict how damage affects behavior.
This project builds mouse models to find out what a phosphorylation site on α-synuclein does.
This project studies how the intestinal epithelium uses membrane trafficking to protect itself from bacteria and viruses.
This project gives computational support for analyzing large environmental health datasets, including exposomics, omics, and electronic health record data.
This project tries to find drugs that block the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor to treat neuropathic pain.
